sections.title: Sound of ú
paragraphs: The letter name is (ú) /uː/. It makes one main vowel sound, as in (út) /ˈuːt/, which means road. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter always has one sound.

sections.title: How to say ú
paragraphs: Pull the back of your tongue high up. Shape your lips into a tight small circle. Turn your voice on so your throat vibrates. Keep your tongue steady and hold the sound longer than a quick vowel. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the strong steady vibration.

sections.title: Reading the letter ú
paragraphs: The accent mark shows that this vowel is long. A long sound is a sound that you hold for more time. In every position you say the letter as in (húsz) /ˈhuːs/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not let this sound become a diphthong like the vowel in the English word boot. A diphthong means two vowel sounds in one syllable where the sound glides from the first to the second. Keep your lips and tongue perfectly still until the sound ends.
